security_audit.summary: The static backtick findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences and JavaScript template literals in examples. The review found contextual risks around broad Copilot tool delegation and sensitive code sent to an external AI service.

remediation.suggestion: Change examples to default allowAllTools to false, and tell users to enable it only for trusted, bounded tasks.

remediation.issue: Sensitive code sharing guidance is incomplete
remediation.suggestion: Add clear guidance to remove secrets and confirm policy approval before sending proprietary code or errors to Copilot.

content.user_title: Use Copilot MCP Tools in Coding Workflows
content.value_statement: Developers need quick access to code review, debugging, and refactoring help without changing workflows. This skill documents Copilot MCP tools for focused AI assistance.
actual_capabilities: Documents the ask-copilot tool with prompt, context, model, and tool access options.
Shows Copilot review, explain, debug, refactor, and test generation tool inputs.
Lists available model choices and the tasks each model targets.
Explains session start and session history tools for continuing related conversations.
Provides examples for implementation help, security review, debugging, and test generation.
limitations: Requires an active GitHub Copilot subscription and working MCP server configuration.
Quality depends on the prompt, provided context, selected model, and Copilot availability.
Code, errors, prompts, and context may be sent to an external AI service.
The skill is documentation only and does not include standalone executable tooling.

use_cases.title: Focused Code Review
use_cases.description: Ask Copilot to review a change for security, performance, maintainability, or best practices before merging.

use_cases.title: Debugging Support
use_cases.description: Provide an error message and relevant context so Copilot can explain likely causes and next steps.
use_cases.target_user: Developer troubleshooting production or test failures

use_cases.title: Test Planning
use_cases.description: Use the test generation guidance to identify important unit test cases for existing functions or modules.

prompt_templates.title: Ask a Basic Coding Question
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a concise technical answer.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use copilot-mcp-server to ask Copilot this question: What is the safest way to handle this coding task? Include assumptions and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Existing Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Copilot explain tool for this code. Summarize its purpose, inputs, outputs, edge cases, and possible risks.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Check a proposed update before review or merge.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Copilot review tool on this change. Focus on security, performance, maintainability, and missing tests.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Refactor With Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for design, refactoring, and validation guidance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Copilot to propose a refactor plan for this module, then identify regression tests and risks before implementation.

output_examples.input: Explain a module that parses user requests and routes them to handlers.
output_examples.output: Copilot returns a plain-language summary of the module purpose, main data flow, important edge cases, and risky assumptions.

output_examples.input: Review an authentication change with security and maintainability focus.
output: Security notes identify password handling and token storage risks.
Maintainability notes flag unclear validation boundaries.
Suggested tests cover failed login, expired sessions, and permission checks.

output_examples.input: Debug a failing API response parser with the error message and context.
output_examples.output: Copilot explains the likely cause, checks assumptions about the response object, and suggests a focused verification path.

best_practices: Provide only the code and context needed for the specific Copilot task.
Choose the smallest capable model for routine explanations or syntax questions.
Keep broad tool access disabled unless the task is trusted and clearly bounded.
anti_patterns: Do not paste secrets, credentials, or proprietary code without approval.
Do not use broad prompts such as write code without requirements or constraints.
Do not enable all tools for prompts that include untrusted or user supplied content.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It documents how to use GitHub Copilot MCP tools for coding questions, reviews, explanations, debugging, refactoring, and tests.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub Copilot?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill states that all tools require an active GitHub Copilot subscription.

faq.question: Can I use it from Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when the MCP tooling is configured.

faq.question: Does the skill run code by itself?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a documentation guide for MCP tool calls and does not include executable scripts.

faq.question: What should I avoid sending to Copilot?
faq.answer: Avoid secrets, credentials, regulated data, and proprietary code unless your organization permits that use.

faq.question: When should I use session tools?
faq.answer: Use session tools when related questions need shared context across multiple Copilot interactions.
